newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian petrol fund to pay VAT on contracts.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian petrol fund to pay VAT on contracts.

text.p: Nigeria's Petroleum Trust Fund (PTF) will have to pay value added tax (VAT) on any contract it awards despite a request for exemption, the national news reported on Wednesday.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) quoted an unnamed official of the national tax department saying the PTF would also have to pay VAT on contracts already awarded.
The PTF was set up to cushion the blow of a four-fold rise in petrol prices in 1994 through social spending. At the beginning of 1996 it amassed over 30 billion naira, it continues to collect money.

It has already awarded contracts for several road repair plans and provided money for the supply of drugs to public hospitals. Military ruler General Sani Abacha said the armed forces would also benefit from the fund.

The PTF wrote to the tax department claiming the law that set up the fund stipulated VAT must be deducted from the proceeds of the 1994 petrol pump price rise to 11 naira a litre. But the official said the VAT deducted from the fuel price was not paid by the PTF, but by the consumers.
